pr_comments: This will start the dev server as well. You could add a prop to the `serve` option to only enable HMR functionality.

I agree, I'm having difficulty browsing the code base because of flowtype IDE support, I installed [this extension ](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=flowtype.flow-for-vscode) which is the [official/recommended extension](https://flow.org/en/docs/editors/vscode/), and [disabled the default JS/TS linting ](https://stackoverflow.com/a/42633555/4178053), so that vscode stops showing TS lint errors in flow, I'm not able go to type definitions, do you use vscode? how did you setup flow?  can you give me some advice on how to setup a flow type IDE environment in vscode? I'll add it to the contributing.md, so future contributors don't have to ask again.

> I installed this extension which is the official/recommended extension, and disabled the default JS/TS linting , so that vscode stops showing TS lint errors in flow,

Exactly that. Cmd-Click on a property does take me to the definition (autocompletion is somhow half-broken though).
Do you see `Flow 0.119.1 (Coverage XX%)` in the status bar at the bottom?

Yeah, I restarted vscode and everything was fine then, vscode used to ask you to restart after installing an extension now it gives a false sense of security.
> You could add a prop to the serve option to only enable HMR functionality.

I was really conflicted on how to extend the `ParcelOptions` and `PluginOptions`, I thought about it for a while, and hope you agree on the change to the options being/making-them the least repetitive/redundant and breaking possible.

issue_context.title: V2: watch command should (optionally?) start HMR server
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report it looks like in Parcel 2, unlike Parcel 1 the `watch` command doesn't start a HMR server despite the mention of `--hmr-port` and `--hmr-host` in the output of `parcel watch --help` ## 🎛 Configuration (.babelrc, package.json, cli command) `parcel watch index.html --public-dir './'` ## 🤔 Expected Behavior Parcel V2's watch command should have the option to start a HMR server like the serve command and V1's watch command. ## 😯 Current Behavior no option to start HMR server with the watch command. also when using `--hmr-port` and `--hmr-host` with the watch command as described in its help page, the parser doesn't accept them: ``` error: unknown option `--hmr-port' error: unknown option `--hmr-host' ``` ## 💁 Possible Solution add the option or make it default behavior to start HMR server and no HTTP server with the watch command. ## 🔦 Context as I [explained](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/issues/4186#issuecomment-596039229) in issue #4186, I'm developing a WebExtension with Parcel V2 and React and I'm trying to get the awesome default support for Fast Refresh of Parcel V2 to work with web pages not served from a server. ## 💻 Code Sample **index.html**: ```html 📦 Parcel
``` **src/index.tsx**: ```js import * as React from "react"; import { render } from "react-dom"; import { Componentx } from "./componentx"; class App extends React.Component { render() { return ( <> ); } } render(, document.getElementById("app")); ``` **src/componentx**: ```js import React from "react"; export function Componentx() { return ( <>
hello good world!
); } ``` ## 🌍 Your Environment | Software | Version(s) | | ---------------- | ---------- | | Parcel | 2.0.0-alpha.3.2 | Node | v13.9.0 | npm/Yarn | 1.22.0 | Operating System | Linux arch-linux-pc 5.5.7-arch1-1 #1 SMP PREEMPT Sat, 29 Feb 2020 19:06:02 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux
comments:
👍 
This usecase was simply forgotten in https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/pull/3918.

review_comments: Why do we need a separate port options? With `parcel serve`, it will be the same as `--port` and with watch we can just use `--port`

so you can start the HMR server on a different port if you need to. I think it's better to keep the `--port` option only for the dev/web server, **also** that way it's explicit and clear to the CLI user that the default port for the HMR server is 1234, the same as the dev Server and where they're coming from, i.e configurable. 

from the output of $ `parcel help watch` and $ `parcel help serve`:
```
--hmr-port <port>    set the port to serve HMR websockets,
   defaults to random if not available (default: 1234)
```
from the output of $ `parcel help serve` : 
```
  -p, --port <port>    set the port to serve on. defaults to 1234 (default: 1234)
```
note that the `(default: 1234)` is added by the commander package.

I think we want to use the value from the CLI option here instead of hardcoding `1234`?
And same goes for `--hmr-port`, that seems to be completely unused.
